name: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
summary: Cloud concepts, Azure architecture and services, management and governance.

domains.name: Cloud Concepts
topics: Benefits: high availability, scalability, reliability, security, manageability

domains.name: Azure Architecture & Services
topics: Regions, availability zones and region pairs
Resource groups, subscriptions and management groups
Compute: VMs, containers, Functions, App Service
Networking: VNets, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, DNS
Identity: Microsoft Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access
Security: RBAC, Zero Trust, defence in depth, Defender for Cloud

domains.name: Azure Management & Governance
domains.summary: Manage costs, governance and resources in Azure.
topics: Cost management, pricing and TCO calculators
Microsoft Purview, Azure Policy and resource locks
Managing resources: portal, CLI, PowerShell, Arc, ARM templates
Monitoring: Advisor, Service Health, Azure Monitor

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop buying hardware every few years and instead pay monthly for the compute it consumes. Which financial shift does this describe?
choices: Moving from a consumption model to a reserved-only model
Moving from depreciation to amortization of servers
Moving from capital expenditure (CapEx) to operational expenditure (OpEx)
questions.explanation: Cloud services are typically billed as ongoing operating costs instead of large up-front capital purchases.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the consumption-based model used by Azure?
choices: You pay only for the number of users in your directory
You must purchase hardware before deploying services
You pay only for the resources you use, with no up-front cost for most services
You pay a fixed annual fee regardless of usage
questions.explanation: Consumption-based pricing means you are billed for what you actually use, with no up-front infrastructure purchase.

questions.prompt: An online ticket seller sees huge demand for a few hours when popular concerts go on sale. Which cloud characteristic lets resources grow and shrink automatically to match this demand?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability to automatically add or remove resources as demand changes.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling?
choices: They are two names for the same thing
Vertical scaling adds CPU or memory to an existing resource; horizontal scaling adds or removes resource instances
Vertical scaling adds instances; horizontal scaling adds CPU or memory
Vertical scaling only applies to storage; horizontal scaling only applies to networking
questions.explanation: Scaling up/down (vertical) changes the size of a resource, while scaling out/in (horizontal) changes the number of instances.

questions.prompt: A team increases the number of virtual machines behind a load balancer from 3 to 6 during peak hours. What type of scaling is this?
questions.explanation: Adding more instances of a resource is horizontal scaling, also called scaling out.

questions.prompt: A database server is resized from 4 vCPUs to 16 vCPUs to handle more queries. What type of scaling is this?
questions.explanation: Increasing the capacity of a single resource is vertical scaling.

questions.prompt: Which cloud deployment model is owned and operated by a cloud provider and shared by many organizations over the internet?
questions.explanation: A public cloud is built, controlled and maintained by a provider and offers services to multiple customers.

questions.prompt: Which cloud deployment model gives an organization complete control over its resources and security but requires it to buy and maintain the hardware?
questions.explanation: A private cloud is used by a single organization, giving full control but also full responsibility for hardware and maintenance.

questions.prompt: A bank keeps sensitive workloads in its own data center but uses Azure for burst capacity and new web apps, with the two environments connected. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines public and private environments and allows data and applications to move between them.

questions.prompt: An organization uses Azure for some workloads and another cloud provider for others. What is this approach called?
questions.explanation: Using services from more than one public cloud provider is a multi-cloud approach.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service lets you manage servers, Kubernetes clusters and databases running on-premises or in other clouds as if they were Azure resources?
questions.explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure management and governance to resources outside Azure, supporting hybrid and multi-cloud scenarios.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run its existing VMware workloads in Azure without re-platforming them. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure VMware Solution runs VMware environments natively on dedicated Azure infrastructure.

questions.prompt: In the infrastructure as a service (IaaS) model, which of the following is the customer responsible for?
choices: The operating system and installed applications
The physical hosts in the datacenter
questions.explanation: With IaaS the provider manages the physical infrastructure, while the customer manages the OS, middleware, apps and data.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which item is ALWAYS the customer's responsibility regardless of the service type?
choices: The data they store and the accounts and identities they use
The physical security of the datacenter
questions.explanation: Customers always remain responsible for their information and data, devices, and accounts and identities.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which item is ALWAYS the cloud provider's responsibility?
choices: The physical datacenter, physical network and physical hosts
questions.explanation: The physical infrastructure is always managed by the cloud provider in IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

questions.prompt: Which service model gives the customer the MOST control over the computing environment?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides the most control because the customer manages the operating system and everything above it.

questions.prompt: Which service model places the MOST responsibility on the cloud provider?
questions.explanation: With SaaS the provider manages nearly everything; the customer mainly manages data, users and access.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to deploy a web application without managing operating system updates or the underlying servers. Which service model fits best?
questions.explanation: PaaS provides a managed environment for building and running apps, so the provider handles the OS and infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A company subscribes to Microsoft 365 for email and office productivity. Which cloud service model is this?
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 is a complete application delivered over the internet, which is SaaS.

questions.prompt: A team migrates an on-premises server to Azure Virtual Machines with minimal changes, a 'lift-and-shift'. Which service model are they using?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Machines are IaaS, which suits lift-and-shift migrations where the OS is managed by the customer.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes serverless computing?
choices: The provider manages the servers and you are typically billed only when your code runs
No servers are used anywhere to run the code
You must provision and patch dedicated servers
It is only available in private clouds
questions.explanation: Serverless abstracts the servers away; the provider manages infrastructure and scales automatically, often charging per execution.

questions.prompt: Azure Functions is an example of which kind of compute?
choices: Infrastructure as a service virtual machines
questions.explanation: Azure Functions runs code in response to events without the need to manage servers.

questions.prompt: What does high availability focus on in the cloud?
choices: Keeping a service running and accessible with minimal downtime
questions.explanation: High availability is about maximizing uptime, often expressed through SLAs such as 99.9% or 99.99%.

questions.prompt: A service has an SLA of 99.99%. Approximately how much downtime does this allow per month?
questions.explanation: 99.99% availability allows roughly 4.3 minutes of downtime in a 30-day month; 99.9% allows about 43 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which SLA percentage allows the LEAST downtime?
questions.explanation: Each additional nine reduces allowed downtime; 99.999% allows only about 26 seconds per month.

questions.prompt: What does reliability mean in the context of cloud design?
choices: The ability to sign in with a single identity
The ability to apply tags to resources
The ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function
The ability to predict monthly costs
questions.explanation: Reliability is the ability to recover from failures and keep functioning, aided by Azure's decentralized global design.

questions.prompt: Which two areas does the cloud benefit of 'predictability' cover?
questions.explanation: Predictability in the cloud focuses on predicting performance (e.g., via autoscaling) and cost (e.g., via pricing tools).

questions.prompt: Which cloud benefit lets an organization deploy resources using templates, scripts or the portal, and get alerts and metrics on them?
questions.explanation: Manageability includes management of the cloud (metrics, autoscaling, alerts) and management in the cloud (portal, CLI, APIs, templates).

questions.prompt: Why can large cloud providers often offer lower prices than an individual company could achieve on its own?
choices: They require long-term contracts for all services
Economies of scale from operating at massive volume
Customers pay for datacenter maintenance directly
questions.explanation: Operating at huge scale lowers per-unit costs for providers, which can be passed on to customers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an operational expenditure (OpEx)?
choices: Paying a monthly bill for virtual machines used
questions.explanation: OpEx is spending on services or products as they are consumed and is typically deducted in the same period.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a characteristic of capital expenditure (CapEx)?
choices: Spending that can be reduced instantly when demand drops
Up-front spending on physical infrastructure that is depreciated over time
questions.explanation: CapEx is up-front investment in physical assets whose value is depreciated over their useful life.

questions.prompt: A company must prove that its cloud environment meets industry regulations such as ISO 27001. Which cloud benefit helps with this?
choices: Security and governance features, including compliance offerings and policies
questions.explanation: The cloud provides governance tools and compliance certifications that help organizations meet regulatory requirements.

questions.prompt: What is a key security advantage of PaaS and SaaS compared to IaaS?
choices: The customer is responsible for physical security
The provider automatically handles OS patching and maintenance
The customer gets full control over the hypervisor
questions.explanation: With PaaS and SaaS, patches and maintenance of the platform are handled by the provider, reducing the customer's burden.

questions.prompt: Which statement about cloud computing is TRUE?
choices: It is available only to large enterprises
It cannot be used for databases
It delivers computing services such as servers, storage and networking over the internet
It requires customers to own the physical servers
questions.explanation: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services over the internet, enabling faster innovation and flexible resources.

questions.prompt: A startup wants to experiment with a new idea and shut it down within a week if it fails, without long-term costs. Which cloud benefit makes this practical?
choices: Requirement to build a private datacenter
Agility through on-demand provisioning and pay-as-you-go pricing
questions.explanation: Resources can be deployed and removed quickly, and you stop paying when you delete them.

questions.prompt: In which service model is the customer responsible for managing the application code and data, but NOT the operating system?
questions.explanation: In PaaS the provider manages the OS and runtime, while the customer manages apps and data.

questions.prompt: In a SaaS model, which responsibility typically remains with the customer?
choices: Managing user accounts, access and the data they put into the service
questions.explanation: Even with SaaS, customers are responsible for their data, identities and access configuration.

questions.prompt: Which deployment model allows an organization to keep regulated data on-premises while using the public cloud for less sensitive workloads?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud lets organizations decide where each workload runs to meet regulatory or security needs.

questions.prompt: What does the term 'fault tolerance' describe?
choices: A system's ability to keep operating even when one or more components fail
Lowering costs by using reserved instances
questions.explanation: A fault-tolerant system continues working when components fail, usually through redundancy.

questions.prompt: What is disaster recovery primarily concerned with?
choices: Restoring services and data after a major outage or catastrophic event
Scaling a website during normal peak hours
questions.explanation: Disaster recovery is about recovering from major events, often using backups and replication to other regions.

questions.prompt: A company is evaluating Azure versus on-premises hosting. Which of these is a cost the company no longer pays directly when moving to a public cloud?
choices: Charges for data transferred out of Azure
Licensing fees for every SaaS seat
Datacenter electricity, cooling and physical security
questions.explanation: In the public cloud, the provider bears the cost of facilities such as power, cooling and physical security.

questions.prompt: Which benefit of the cloud refers to the ability to deploy applications in regions around the world close to customers?
questions.explanation: Cloud providers operate datacenters worldwide, allowing apps to be deployed near users for lower latency.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a public cloud characteristic?
choices: Only one organization can use the hardware
No capital expenditure is needed to scale up
The organization owns all the hardware
Hardware must be purchased before use
questions.explanation: Public cloud resources can be scaled without buying hardware; you pay for what you use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a private cloud compared to a public cloud?
choices: Higher up-front costs for hardware and ongoing maintenance
It is shared with other organizations
questions.explanation: Private clouds require purchasing and maintaining hardware, which increases cost and management effort.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system on an Azure virtual machine?
questions.explanation: Azure VMs are IaaS, so the customer is responsible for maintaining and patching the guest OS.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the operating system of Azure App Service web apps?
questions.explanation: Azure App Service is PaaS, so Microsoft manages the underlying OS and platform.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility varies by service model and may be shared between the customer and Microsoft?
questions.explanation: Identity and directory infrastructure, applications, network controls and the OS are responsibilities that vary by service type.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic means an organization can obtain more resources whenever needed without contacting the provider?
questions.explanation: On-demand self-service lets customers provision resources themselves, typically through a portal or API, without human interaction.

questions.prompt: Which is the BEST description of the consumption-based model's benefit for unpredictable workloads?
choices: You get a fixed monthly price no matter how much you use
You avoid paying for idle capacity you provisioned for peak demand
You are charged only once per year
You must forecast peak demand years in advance
questions.explanation: With consumption pricing, costs track usage, so you don't pay for unused capacity sized for peaks.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of an Azure service-level agreement (SLA)?
choices: To list the prices of all Azure services
To describe Microsoft's commitments for uptime and connectivity and any service credits if they are not met
To specify the regions where data is stored
To define user permissions in a subscription
questions.explanation: An SLA documents uptime and connectivity commitments and the service credits offered if they are not met.

questions.prompt: A company runs two VMs across two availability zones. Compared to a single VM, what typically happens to the SLA?
choices: SLAs do not apply to virtual machines
The composite deployment qualifies for a higher SLA
questions.explanation: Deploying across multiple availability zones increases redundancy and qualifies VMs for a higher SLA than a single instance.

questions.prompt: If an application depends on two services that each have a 99.9% SLA, what is the approximate composite SLA?
questions.explanation: Composite SLA is the product of the SLAs: 0.999 x 0.999 is about 0.998, or 99.8%.

questions.prompt: Which statement about SLAs for free or preview Azure services is generally TRUE?
choices: Free tiers and preview services typically do not carry a financially backed SLA
They have higher SLAs than paid services
questions.explanation: Preview features and free tiers are usually excluded from SLAs.

questions.prompt: Which cloud service model is BEST suited for a company that wants to host a custom application but avoid managing middleware and runtime?
questions.explanation: PaaS manages the OS, middleware and runtime, so developers focus on code and data.

questions.prompt: An organization wants employees to use a cloud-hosted CRM application without writing any code or managing infrastructure. Which model fits?
questions.explanation: SaaS delivers a ready-to-use application; the customer only configures and uses it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the public cloud is FALSE?
choices: Many organizations share the provider's infrastructure
Customers pay for what they use
Customers must replace failed hardware themselves
questions.explanation: In the public cloud, the provider, not the customer, maintains and replaces physical hardware.

questions.prompt: A retailer needs its website to stay online even if an entire datacenter loses power. Which design approach helps most?
choices: Deploying the app across multiple availability zones
Using a larger single virtual machine
Using a single locally redundant storage account
questions.explanation: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters, so spreading across them protects against a single datacenter failure.

questions.prompt: What does 'agility' mean as a benefit of cloud computing?
choices: Costs are fixed for the life of the contract
Resources can be deployed and configured quickly as requirements change
Data never leaves the customer's premises
questions.explanation: Cloud agility lets teams provision and change resources in minutes rather than weeks.

questions.prompt: Which Azure capability supports predictable performance by automatically adding instances when CPU usage is high?
questions.explanation: Autoscale adjusts capacity based on metrics, helping keep performance predictable under changing load.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the serverless billing model in Azure Functions on a Consumption plan?
choices: You are charged only for storage used by the code
You pay for a dedicated VM 24/7
You pay a fixed fee per developer
You are charged based on executions and resource consumption while the code runs
questions.explanation: On the Consumption plan, Functions bills per execution and execution time/memory, scaling to zero when idle.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of 'management in the cloud' rather than 'management of the cloud'?
choices: Autoscaling a resource based on demand
Using the Azure portal, CLI or APIs to deploy and configure resources
Monitoring resource health and triggering alerts
questions.explanation: Management in the cloud covers how you manage resources, such as through the portal, CLI, APIs or templates.

questions.prompt: Which cloud model most commonly requires the organization to handle all hardware upgrades and capacity planning?
questions.explanation: In a private cloud the organization owns the hardware and must plan, buy and upgrade capacity itself.

questions.prompt: What is an Azure region?
choices: A single server rack in a datacenter
A billing boundary for an organization
A geographical area containing one or more datacenters networked together with low latency
questions.explanation: A region is a geographic area with at least one, and usually several, nearby datacenters connected by a low-latency network.

questions.prompt: What are Azure availability zones?
choices: Pairs of regions in different countries
Physically separate datacenter locations within a region, each with independent power, cooling and networking
Edge locations used for content caching
Logical groups of VMs in one rack
questions.explanation: Availability zones are unique physical locations within a region that protect against datacenter-level failures.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of availability zones in a region that supports them?
questions.explanation: Zone-enabled regions have a minimum of three separate availability zones.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure region pairs is TRUE?
choices: Region pairs are used only for billing
Every region is paired with every other region
Paired regions are typically at least 300 miles apart and updates are rolled out to one region of a pair at a time
Paired regions are always in the same datacenter
questions.explanation: Region pairs are separated geographically and Microsoft sequences planned updates so only one region in a pair is updated at a time.

questions.prompt: During a broad outage affecting multiple regions, what benefit do region pairs provide?
choices: Data is automatically deleted from both regions
Microsoft prioritizes recovery of one region in each pair
Both regions in a pair are always restored first
questions.explanation: In a widespread outage, recovery of at least one region from each pair is prioritized.

questions.prompt: What are Azure sovereign regions?
choices: Regions that have no availability zones
Instances of Azure isolated from the main Azure cloud for compliance or legal reasons, such as Azure Government
Regions available only to Microsoft employees
questions.explanation: Sovereign regions such as Azure Government (US) and Azure operated by 21Vianet (China) are isolated for legal and compliance needs.

questions.prompt: Which Azure offering is designed for US government agencies and their partners?
questions.explanation: Azure Government is a sovereign cloud physically isolated for US federal, state and local government use.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Azure resource groups and resources?
choices: A resource can belong to several resource groups at once
Each resource exists in exactly one resource group at a time
Resource groups can be nested inside other resource groups
Resources can exist without any resource group
questions.explanation: Every resource must be in one, and only one, resource group, and resource groups cannot be nested.

questions.prompt: What happens when you delete a resource group?
choices: All resources inside the resource group are also deleted
Resources are moved to the subscription root
Only the empty resource group is removed and resources move to another group
Nothing happens until each resource is deleted individually
questions.explanation: Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it, which makes groups handy for managing lifecycles together.

questions.prompt: Which statement about resource groups is TRUE?
choices: A resource group can span multiple subscriptions
All resources in a group must be in the same region
A resource group can contain resources from different regions
questions.explanation: A resource group has a location for its metadata, but the resources inside it can be in any region.

questions.prompt: Which hierarchy correctly orders Azure scopes from broadest to narrowest?
choices: Resource groups > subscriptions > management groups > resources
Resources > resource groups > subscriptions > management groups
Subscriptions > management groups > resources > resource groups
Management groups > subscriptions > resource groups > resources
questions.explanation: Management groups contain subscriptions, which contain resource groups, which contain resources.

questions.prompt: What are Azure subscriptions used for?
choices: They act as a billing and access-management boundary for Azure resources
questions.explanation: Subscriptions provide authenticated, authorized access to Azure and are a unit of billing and management.

questions.prompt: A company wants separate invoices for its Development and Production environments. What is the simplest approach?
choices: Put both in one resource group with different tags only
Create separate subscriptions for each environment
questions.explanation: Subscriptions are billing boundaries, so separate subscriptions produce separate billing and access control.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Azure management groups?
choices: To route traffic between virtual networks
To organize multiple subscriptions and apply governance such as policies and access to them
To group virtual machines for load balancing
questions.explanation: Management groups let you manage access, policy and compliance across many subscriptions at once.

questions.prompt: Which statement about management groups is TRUE?
choices: Management groups can be nested to create a hierarchy
Management groups cannot have policies assigned
A subscription can belong to multiple management groups
Management groups can contain individual VMs directly
questions.explanation: Management groups support a nested hierarchy (up to six levels below the root), and each subscription has a single parent.

questions.prompt: Which Azure compute service provides the most control over the operating system and installed software?
questions.explanation: VMs are IaaS and give full control over the OS, configuration and installed software.

questions.prompt: A company needs a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that automatically increase in number as demand grows. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: Scale sets create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that can autoscale.

questions.prompt: What do availability sets use to protect VMs within a datacenter?
questions.explanation: Availability sets spread VMs across fault domains (separate power/network) and update domains (staggered maintenance).

questions.prompt: In an availability set, what is the purpose of update domains?
choices: To control who can update a VM
To ensure only a group of VMs is rebooted at a time during planned maintenance
To store VM updates in a storage account
To separate VMs across different regions
questions.explanation: Update domains group VMs that can be rebooted together, so not all VMs go down during maintenance.

questions.prompt: In an availability set, what is the purpose of fault domains?
choices: To assign VMs to different users
To group VMs that share a common power source and network switch so a hardware failure affects only some VMs
To separate VMs into different subscriptions
questions.explanation: Fault domains spread VMs across separate racks with independent power and networking.

questions.prompt: A company wants employees to access a full Windows desktop and apps from any device, hosted in Azure. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop provides virtualized Windows desktops and apps hosted in Azure.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Virtual Desktop feature lets multiple users sign in to the same session host at the same time?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop supports Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session, allowing many concurrent users per VM.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to run a single container quickly without managing VMs or an orchestrator. Which service is the BEST fit?
questions.explanation: Azure Container Instances is the fastest, simplest way to run a container in Azure as a PaaS offering.

questions.prompt: Which service should a company use to orchestrate many containers with automated scaling, rolling updates and self-healing?
questions.explanation: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service for orchestrating containerized applications at scale.

questions.prompt: Compared with virtual machines, what is a key advantage of containers?
choices: Each container includes its own full guest OS
They are lightweight and start quickly because they share the host OS kernel
They cannot be moved between environments
questions.explanation: Containers package an app with its dependencies but share the host kernel, so they are smaller and start faster than VMs.

questions.prompt: Which service is BEST for running a small piece of code whenever a message arrives in a queue, without managing servers?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is event-driven serverless compute that can trigger on queue messages, timers, HTTP requests and more.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between stateless and stateful (Durable) Azure Functions?
choices: Stateful functions cannot be triggered by HTTP
Stateless functions start fresh each run; Durable Functions keep context across steps of a workflow
questions.explanation: By default functions are stateless; the Durable Functions extension lets them maintain state across executions.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service provides a fully managed platform for hosting web apps, REST APIs and mobile back ends?
questions.explanation: App Service is a PaaS offering for hosting web apps, APIs and mobile back ends in many languages.

questions.prompt: What is an Azure Virtual Network (VNet) used for?
choices: To let Azure resources communicate securely with each other, the internet and on-premises networks
questions.explanation: VNets provide isolation and segmentation and enable communication among Azure resources, the internet and on-premises networks.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of subnets in an Azure virtual network?
choices: To segment a VNet's address space into smaller ranges for organizing and securing resources
questions.explanation: Subnets divide a VNet into segments so you can group resources and apply security rules.

questions.prompt: Two virtual networks in different Azure regions need to communicate privately using Microsoft's backbone. Which feature should be used?
choices: A public IP address on every VM
questions.explanation: VNet peering connects VNets, and global peering connects VNets across regions over the Microsoft backbone network.

questions.prompt: When two VNets are peered, how does traffic between them travel?
choices: Over the Microsoft backbone network, not the public internet
questions.explanation: Peered VNet traffic stays private on Microsoft's backbone infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Which resource can you use to filter inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources in a subnet based on IP address, port and protocol?
questions.explanation: NSGs contain security rules that allow or deny traffic based on source, destination, port and protocol.

questions.prompt: A company needs an encrypted connection from its on-premises network to Azure over the public internet. Which service should it use?
choices: Azure VPN Gateway with a site-to-site VPN
questions.explanation: VPN Gateway creates encrypted IPsec/IKE tunnels over the internet between on-premises and Azure.

questions.prompt: Which VPN type connects an individual remote computer to an Azure virtual network?
questions.explanation: Point-to-site VPN connects individual devices to a VNet.

questions.prompt: A company needs a private, dedicated connection to Azure that does NOT travel over the public internet, with predictable latency. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute provides private connections via a connectivity provider and does not traverse the public internet.

questions.prompt: Which statement about ExpressRoute is TRUE?
choices: It always routes traffic over the public internet
It can connect on-premises networks to Microsoft cloud services such as Azure and Microsoft 365
It is used only to connect two Azure VNets
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute extends on-premises networks into the Microsoft cloud, including Azure and Microsoft 365.

questions.prompt: What does Azure DNS provide?
choices: Hosting of DNS domains using Microsoft's global infrastructure for name resolution
questions.explanation: Azure DNS hosts DNS zones and resolves names using Azure's global network of name servers.

questions.prompt: Which capability lets an Azure virtual network resolve custom domain names for resources inside it without exposing them publicly?
questions.explanation: Private DNS zones provide name resolution within VNets without exposing records to the internet.

questions.prompt: What is a private endpoint in Azure?
choices: A network interface with a private IP from your VNet that connects privately to a PaaS service
A URL for downloading the Azure CLI
A public IP address assigned to a VM
A firewall rule in a network security group
questions.explanation: Private endpoints use a private IP in your VNet, bringing a service such as Azure Storage into your network via Private Link.

questions.prompt: Which service allows access to Azure PaaS services over a private endpoint in your virtual network?
questions.explanation: Azure Private Link enables private access to Azure services over a private endpoint so traffic stays off the public internet.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a public endpoint and a private endpoint for an Azure service?
choices: A public endpoint is reachable via a public IP address; a private endpoint uses a private IP inside your VNet
Public endpoints are always encrypted and private ones are not
There is no difference in how they are reached
Private endpoints can only be used by Microsoft
questions.explanation: Public endpoints are internet-reachable, while private endpoints place the service on a private IP in your VNet.

questions.prompt: An administrator needs secure RDP/SSH access to Azure VMs without assigning public IP addresses to them. Which service should be used?
questions.explanation: Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH over TLS directly from the portal, without exposing VMs via public IPs.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Storage service is optimized for storing massive amounts of unstructured data such as images, videos and backups?
questions.explanation: Blob Storage is object storage for unstructured data such as text, images, video and backups.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Storage service provides fully managed file shares accessible via SMB or NFS?
questions.explanation: Azure Files offers managed file shares accessible using SMB and NFS protocols.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Storage service is used to store messages for asynchronous communication between application components?
questions.explanation: Queue Storage stores large numbers of messages that can be processed asynchronously.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Storage service stores structured, non-relational (NoSQL) key/attribute data?
questions.explanation: Table Storage stores schemaless structured NoSQL data in key/attribute form.

questions.prompt: What type of storage do Azure Virtual Machines use for their operating system and data volumes?
questions.explanation: Azure Disk Storage provides block-level managed disks for VMs.

questions.prompt: Which Blob Storage access tier is best for data that is accessed frequently?
questions.explanation: The Hot tier has the highest storage cost but the lowest access cost, suited to frequently accessed data.

questions.prompt: Which Blob Storage access tier has the lowest storage cost but requires rehydration that can take hours before data can be read?
questions.explanation: Archive is offline storage with the cheapest storage cost; blobs must be rehydrated before they can be read.

questions.prompt: Data must be kept for compliance but is accessed only a few times a year and must be readable immediately when needed. Which tier is the most cost-effective choice among these?
questions.explanation: Cold is an online tier for rarely accessed data (stored at least 90 days) that remains immediately readable, unlike Archive.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended minimum storage duration for data in the Cool tier to avoid an early deletion charge?
questions.explanation: Cool tier has a 30-day minimum, Cold 90 days and Archive 180 days.

questions.prompt: Which redundancy option stores three copies of data within a single datacenter in the primary region?
questions.explanation: LRS replicates data three times within one datacenter and is the lowest-cost option.

questions.prompt: Which redundancy option replicates data synchronously across three availability zones in the primary region?
questions.explanation: ZRS keeps copies in three separate availability zones within the primary region.

questions.prompt: Which redundancy option copies data to a secondary region and uses LRS in BOTH the primary and secondary regions?
questions.explanation: GRS uses LRS in the primary region and asynchronously replicates to LRS in the secondary region.

questions.prompt: Which redundancy option combines zone redundancy in the primary region with replication to a secondary region?
questions.explanation: GZRS uses ZRS in the primary region and replicates asynchronously to a secondary region.

questions.prompt: An application must be able to READ data from the secondary region even when the primary region is available. Which option enables this?
questions.explanation: With GRS/GZRS the secondary is readable only after failover; RA-GRS and RA-GZRS allow reads from the secondary at any time.

questions.prompt: Which storage redundancy option offers the LOWEST cost but the least durability?
questions.explanation: LRS is the cheapest because all copies are in one datacenter, so it doesn't protect against datacenter or regional failures.

questions.prompt: Which command-line utility is used to copy blobs or files to or from a storage account?
questions.explanation: AzCopy is a command-line tool for copying data to, from and between storage accounts.

questions.prompt: Which tool provides a graphical user interface for managing files and blobs in Azure Storage from Windows, macOS or Linux?
questions.explanation: Storage Explorer is a standalone GUI app for managing storage account data across platforms.

questions.prompt: A company wants to keep using its Windows file servers on-premises while centralizing file shares in Azure Files with local caching. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Azure File Sync turns Windows Server into a cache of Azure file shares and can tier cold files to the cloud.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a central hub to discover, assess and migrate on-premises servers, databases and web apps to Azure?
questions.explanation: Azure Migrate offers tools for discovery, assessment and migration of on-premises workloads.

questions.prompt: A company needs to transfer 60 TB of data to Azure but has very limited bandwidth. Which service is BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure Data Box is a physical, ruggedized device shipped to you for moving large amounts of data offline.

questions.prompt: Besides importing data into Azure, what else can Azure Data Box be used for?
choices: Exporting large amounts of data from Azure to on-premises, such as for disaster recovery
questions.explanation: Data Box supports both import to and export from Azure for large data sets.

questions.prompt: What is a storage account in Azure?
choices: A virtual network for storage traffic
A unique namespace that holds your Azure Storage data objects such as blobs, files, queues and tables
A user account for Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explanation: A storage account provides a globally unique namespace for your storage data that is accessible over HTTP/HTTPS.

questions.prompt: Which requirement applies to Azure storage account names?
choices: They can include uppercase letters and spaces
They must be globally unique across Azure
They must be unique only within a subscription
They must match the resource group name
questions.explanation: Storage account names must be globally unique, 3-24 characters, and use only lowercase letters and numbers.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) manages identities, authentication and access to resources.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra feature lets users sign in once and access many applications without signing in again?
questions.explanation: SSO allows one set of credentials to access multiple applications.

questions.prompt: What does multifactor authentication (MFA) require?
choices: Signing in from two devices simultaneously
Two or more forms of verification, such as something you know, have or are
questions.explanation: MFA requires multiple factors, such as a password plus a phone notification or biometric.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a passwordless authentication method supported by Microsoft Entra ID?
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business, Microsoft Authenticator and FIDO2 security keys are passwordless methods.

questions.prompt: A company wants partners from another organization to access its SharePoint site using the partners' own credentials. Which feature fits?
choices: Microsoft Entra External ID for customers (B2C)
questions.explanation: B2B collaboration lets external users sign in with their own identities to access your apps and resources as guests.

questions.prompt: A retailer wants customers to sign up for its mobile app using social accounts such as Google or Facebook. Which identity solution fits?
choices: Customer identity and access management (B2C) via Microsoft Entra External ID
questions.explanation: B2C-style customer identity lets consumers sign up and sign in to your apps with local or social accounts.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra feature evaluates signals such as user, location and device to decide whether to allow access, require MFA or block?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access uses if-then policies based on identity signals to enforce access decisions.

questions.prompt: Which service provides managed domain services such as domain join, group policy and Kerberos authentication without deploying domain controllers?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed AD DS-compatible features for legacy apps.

questions.prompt: Which tool synchronizes on-premises Active Directory identities with Microsoft Entra ID?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect (and Cloud Sync) synchronizes users and groups from on-premises AD to Entra ID.

questions.prompt: What does Azure role-based access control (RBAC) allow you to do?
choices: Prevent resources from being deleted regardless of permissions
Restrict which regions resources can be deployed to
Grant users only the permissions they need at a specific scope
questions.explanation: Azure RBAC assigns roles to security principals at scopes such as management group, subscription, resource group or resource.

questions.prompt: A role is assigned to a user at the subscription scope. Which resources does the user's access apply to?
choices: Only resources in the same region as the user
Only resources created after the assignment
All resource groups and resources within that subscription
questions.explanation: RBAC assignments are inherited by child scopes, so a subscription assignment applies to everything beneath it.

questions.prompt: Which built-in Azure RBAC role can manage all resources but CANNOT grant access to others?
questions.explanation: Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles; Owner can do both.

questions.prompt: Which principle is central to the Zero Trust security model?
choices: Trust everything inside the corporate network
Grant broad admin rights to reduce help desk calls
Never trust, always verify, and assume breach
Allow all traffic from known IP ranges
questions.explanation: Zero Trust verifies explicitly, uses least-privilege access and assumes breach, rather than trusting the network perimeter.

questions.prompt: What is defense in depth?
choices: Encrypting only the most sensitive data
A layered approach to security so that if one layer is breached, other layers still protect the data
Relying entirely on the cloud provider for security
Using a single very strong firewall
questions.explanation: Defense in depth uses multiple layers, such as physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application and data.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer is at the CENTER, being the asset ultimately protected?
questions.explanation: Data is the innermost layer; the other layers exist to protect it.

questions.prompt: Which defense-in-depth layer focuses on controlling access to infrastructure and change control, for example with SSO and MFA?
questions.explanation: The identity and access layer ensures identities are secure and access is granted only as needed.

questions.prompt: Which service provides distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) mitigation for Azure resources at the perimeter layer?
questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection helps protect resources from DDoS attacks at the perimeter.

questions.prompt: Which service securely stores and manages secrets, encryption keys and certificates?
questions.explanation: Key Vault centralizes storage of secrets, keys and certificates with access policies and auditing.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
choices: A service that issues TLS certificates
A cloud security posture management and workload protection tool for Azure, hybrid and multi-cloud resources
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud assesses security posture, gives a secure score and recommendations, and protects workloads across environments.

questions.prompt: Which factor typically affects the cost of an Azure virtual machine?
choices: The VM size, region and how long it runs
The name of the resource group
questions.explanation: Resource type and size, consumption and location (region) are key factors in Azure costs.

questions.prompt: Why might the same Azure service cost different amounts in two regions?
choices: Prices can vary by region due to local costs such as power, taxes and demand
Region pricing depends on the number of users in your tenant
Only sovereign regions charge for services
questions.explanation: Azure pricing differs by region, so location is a cost factor.

questions.prompt: Which type of network traffic is generally NOT charged in Azure?
choices: Inbound data transfer into Azure datacenters
Outbound data transfer through a VPN gateway
Outbound data transfer from Azure to the internet
questions.explanation: Ingress (data into Azure) is generally free, while egress and inter-region transfer usually incur charges.

questions.prompt: A company runs VMs 24/7 for a stable workload for the next three years. Which option can significantly reduce cost?
choices: Moving to the Archive storage tier
questions.explanation: Reserved instances give a discount in exchange for a one- or three-year commitment.

questions.prompt: A company with existing Windows Server and SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance wants to reduce VM costs in Azure. What should it use?
questions.explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you reuse eligible on-premises licenses in Azure to lower costs.

questions.prompt: Which option offers deep discounts for VMs running interruptible workloads, such as batch jobs, but can be evicted when Azure needs capacity?
questions.explanation: Spot VMs use unused capacity at a discount but can be evicted at any time.

questions.prompt: Which tool estimates the monthly cost of Azure services you plan to deploy?
questions.explanation: The Pricing calculator estimates the cost of provisioning specific Azure resources.

questions.prompt: Which tool compares the cost of running workloads on-premises with the cost of running them in Azure over time?
questions.explanation: The TCO calculator compares on-premises infrastructure costs, such as servers, power and labor, with Azure.

questions.prompt: When using the TCO calculator, which of the following would you typically enter?
choices: Your Microsoft Entra ID tenant name
Details about current on-premises servers, databases, storage and networking
The resource locks you plan to use
questions.explanation: The TCO calculator takes on-premises workload details and assumptions such as power and IT labor costs.

questions.prompt: Which service helps you analyze Azure spending, set budgets and receive alerts when costs exceed thresholds?
questions.explanation: Cost Management provides cost analysis, budgets and alerts for Azure spending.

questions.prompt: A finance team wants an email when monthly spending in a subscription reaches 80% of a defined amount. What should be configured?
choices: A budget with an alert in Cost Management
questions.explanation: Budgets in Cost Management can trigger alerts at defined spending thresholds.

questions.prompt: Which type of Cost Management alert notifies you when Azure credits for an Enterprise Agreement are being consumed?
questions.explanation: Cost Management offers budget alerts, credit alerts and department spending quota alerts.

questions.prompt: What are tags in Azure?
choices: Security rules that block network traffic
Name/value pairs applied to resources to organize them, for example by cost center or environment
questions.explanation: Tags are metadata name/value pairs used for organization, cost reporting and automation.

questions.prompt: A company wants to see Azure costs broken down by department. What is a straightforward way to enable this?
choices: Use a single availability zone per department
Apply a tag such as CostCenter to resources and group costs by that tag
Put all resources in one resource group
Create a resource lock per department
questions.explanation: Tags let you filter and group cost reports by values such as department or cost center.

questions.prompt: Are tags on a resource group automatically inherited by the resources inside it?
choices: No, tags are not inherited by default, though Azure Policy can enforce or copy them
questions.explanation: Resources do not inherit tags from their resource group or subscription by default; policies can apply them.

questions.prompt: How can an organization require that every new resource has an Environment tag?
choices: Assign an Azure Policy that requires the tag
questions.explanation: Azure Policy can require tags or add them automatically during deployment.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Azure Policy?
choices: To create, assign and enforce rules so that resources stay compliant with corporate standards
To grant users permissions to resources
questions.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates resources against rules and can deny, audit or modify non-compliant resources.

questions.prompt: A company must ensure that resources are deployed only in West Europe and North Europe. What should it use?
choices: Azure Policy with an allowed locations definition
questions.explanation: The built-in Allowed locations policy restricts which regions resources can be deployed to.

questions.prompt: What is an Azure Policy initiative?
choices: A group of related policy definitions managed together toward a goal
questions.explanation: Initiatives bundle policy definitions, such as those needed for a compliance standard, for easier assignment.

questions.prompt: How does Azure Policy differ from Azure RBAC?
choices: RBAC is used only for billing
Policy controls which resource properties are allowed; RBAC controls which actions users can perform
questions.explanation: RBAC focuses on user actions at a scope, while Policy focuses on resource properties and compliance.

questions.prompt: If an Azure Policy is assigned at a management group, which resources does it apply to?
choices: Only resources in the same region
Only the management group object itself
Only resources created by the policy author
All subscriptions, resource groups and resources under that management group
questions.explanation: Policy assignments are inherited by all child scopes.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy capability can automatically fix existing non-compliant resources?
questions.explanation: Remediation tasks can bring existing resources into compliance for policies with deployIfNotExists or modify effects.

questions.prompt: What do resource locks protect against?
choices: Accidental deletion or modification of resources
questions.explanation: Locks prevent resources from being accidentally deleted or changed, even by users with permissions.

questions.prompt: Which lock type allows users to read and modify a resource but not delete it?
questions.explanation: A CanNotDelete lock lets authorized users modify a resource but prevents deletion.

questions.prompt: Which lock type prevents both deleting and modifying a resource?
questions.explanation: A ReadOnly lock is like granting everyone Reader permission on the resource.

questions.prompt: An administrator with the Owner role tries to delete a resource with a CanNotDelete lock. What happens?
choices: The resource moves to another resource group
The deletion fails until the lock is removed
The resource is deleted because Owners bypass locks
questions.explanation: Locks apply to everyone, including Owners; the lock must be removed first.

questions.prompt: A lock is applied to a resource group. What is the effect on resources in the group?
choices: Only the resource group is locked, not its resources
The lock is ignored for VMs
Resources are moved out of the group
questions.explanation: Locks applied at a parent scope are inherited by all resources at that scope.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Purview?
choices: A family of data governance, risk and compliance solutions for discovering, classifying and protecting data
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview helps organizations govern, protect and manage data across on-premises, multi-cloud and SaaS environments.

questions.prompt: A company wants a unified map of its data across on-premises, Azure and other clouds, with automated data classification and lineage. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Purview's data governance capabilities create a map of data with discovery, classification and lineage.

questions.prompt: Which portal provides access to Microsoft's audit reports, compliance documentation and trust information?
questions.explanation: The Service Trust Portal provides reports and documents about Microsoft's security, privacy and compliance practices.

questions.prompt: What is the Azure portal?
choices: A command-line tool installed only on Linux
A web-based, unified console for building, managing and monitoring Azure resources
questions.explanation: The Azure portal is a browser-based interface for managing Azure resources.

questions.prompt: What is Azure Cloud Shell?
choices: A tool that only works on Windows
A browser-based shell that provides Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell without local installation
A VM that you must create first
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell is an authenticated, browser-accessible shell supporting Bash and PowerShell.

questions.prompt: Which two shell experiences does Azure Cloud Shell offer?
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell supports both Bash (with Azure CLI) and PowerShell (with Azure PowerShell).

questions.prompt: Which tool is a set of cmdlets for managing Azure resources from PowerShell?
questions.explanation: Azure PowerShell provides cmdlets that call the Azure REST API to manage resources.

questions.prompt: Which cross-platform command-line tool uses commands such as 'az vm create' to manage Azure?
questions.explanation: The Azure CLI uses Bash-style commands that begin with 'az'.

questions.prompt: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?
choices: The deployment and management service that processes all requests to create, update and delete Azure resources
questions.explanation: ARM is the management layer; all tools such as the portal, CLI and PowerShell send requests through it.

questions.prompt: Why do requests from the portal, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell produce consistent results?
choices: They run in the same browser
They each use a separate API
They use the same storage account
They all go through Azure Resource Manager
questions.explanation: ARM provides a consistent management layer for all tools and SDKs.

questions.prompt: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)?
choices: Writing application code that runs in containers
Managing and provisioning infrastructure through declarative files instead of manual processes
questions.explanation: IaC defines infrastructure in code files, enabling repeatable, consistent deployments.

questions.prompt: Which two formats can be used to write Azure Resource Manager templates?
questions.explanation: ARM templates are written in JSON, and Bicep is a domain-specific language that compiles to ARM JSON.

questions.prompt: What is a benefit of the declarative syntax used by ARM templates and Bicep?
choices: Templates can deploy only one resource
You must write every step in order
You describe what you want to deploy without writing the sequence of commands to create it
questions.explanation: Declarative templates state the desired result, and ARM figures out how to deploy it.

questions.prompt: What happens if you deploy the same ARM template multiple times to the same environment?
choices: The deployment always fails the second time
You get the same resources in the same state, because deployments are idempotent
questions.explanation: ARM template deployments are idempotent, producing consistent results on repeated runs.

questions.prompt: Which language is a newer, more concise alternative to JSON for authoring ARM templates?
questions.explanation: Bicep is a declarative language that offers simpler syntax and transpiles to ARM JSON.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure Arc is TRUE?
choices: It is a type of storage redundancy
It migrates data on physical disks
It lets you manage non-Azure servers using Azure tools such as Azure Policy and RBAC
questions.explanation: Azure Arc projects external resources into Azure Resource Manager so you can govern them consistently.

questions.prompt: A company wants to apply Azure Policy to Linux servers running in another cloud provider. Which service enables this?
questions.explanation: Arc-enabled servers can be governed by Azure Policy just like Azure VMs.

questions.prompt: Which types of resources can Azure Arc manage outside Azure?
choices: Servers, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services and SQL Server
questions.explanation: Azure Arc supports servers, Kubernetes, Azure data services, SQL Server and VMs running on-premises or in other clouds.

questions.prompt: What does Azure Advisor do?
choices: It analyzes your deployed resources and gives personalized recommendations to optimize them
questions.explanation: Advisor evaluates resources and recommends improvements for reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence.

questions.prompt: Which categories does Azure Advisor provide recommendations in?
choices: Reliability, security, performance, operational excellence and cost
questions.explanation: Advisor organizes recommendations into these five categories.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants a recommendation on which underused VMs could be resized or shut down to save money. Which tool provides this?
questions.explanation: Advisor's cost recommendations identify underused resources such as idle VMs.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a personalized view of Azure service issues, planned maintenance and health advisories that affect YOUR resources?
questions.explanation: Service Health focuses on the Azure services and regions you use and can send alerts.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between Azure status and Azure Service Health?
choices: Azure status shows global service health for everyone; Service Health shows issues specific to your services and regions
Azure status is only available to Owners
Service Health is used only for billing
questions.explanation: Azure status is a broad global view, while Service Health is personalized for your subscriptions.

questions.prompt: Which component of Azure Service Health shows the health of your individual resources, such as whether a specific VM is available?
questions.explanation: Resource Health reports the current and past health of individual resources.

questions.prompt: Which service collects and analyzes metrics and logs from Azure and on-premises environments to help you understand performance?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor is a comprehensive platform for collecting, analyzing and acting on telemetry.

questions.prompt: Which tool in the Azure portal lets you write and run queries against log data collected by Azure Monitor?
questions.explanation: Log Analytics lets you edit and run Kusto (KQL) queries on Azure Monitor Logs.

questions.prompt: Which query language is used in Log Analytics?
questions.explanation: Log Analytics queries use KQL.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Monitor feature monitors the performance and usage of live web applications, such as request rates, response times and failures?
questions.explanation: Application Insights is an Azure Monitor feature for application performance monitoring.

questions.prompt: Application Insights can monitor web applications hosted where?
choices: In Azure, on-premises or in another cloud
questions.explanation: Application Insights works for apps hosted anywhere, as long as they are instrumented.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to be notified when a VM's CPU exceeds 90% for 10 minutes. What should they configure?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor alerts notify you when metric or log conditions are met.

questions.prompt: What can Azure Monitor alerts do besides sending an email?
choices: Trigger automated actions through action groups, such as running a Logic App or Function
questions.explanation: Action groups define notifications and automated actions like webhooks, Functions or Logic Apps.

questions.prompt: Which log in Azure records subscription-level events, such as who created or deleted a resource and when?
questions.explanation: The Azure activity log records control-plane operations performed on resources.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure Policy compliance is TRUE?
choices: Azure Policy shows a compliance dashboard indicating which resources are non-compliant
It only applies to storage accounts
It can only evaluate resources at creation time and never again
questions.explanation: Policy continuously evaluates resources and reports compliance status.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy effect blocks a resource from being created if it does not meet the rule?
questions.explanation: The Deny effect prevents a non-compliant resource request from succeeding.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy effect creates a warning in the activity log for non-compliant resources but does NOT block them?
questions.explanation: Audit flags non-compliance without preventing deployment.

questions.prompt: What is a valid way to reduce Azure storage costs for blobs that are rarely accessed over time?
choices: Use lifecycle management rules to move blobs to cooler tiers automatically
Add more tags to the blobs
Apply a ReadOnly lock to the account
questions.explanation: Lifecycle management policies can transition blobs to Cool, Cold or Archive tiers based on age.

questions.prompt: Which action is MOST likely to reduce costs for development VMs that are only used during business hours?
choices: Apply GZRS storage to their disks
Configure auto-shutdown or stop (deallocate) them outside working hours
Add them to an availability set
Upgrade them to larger VM sizes
questions.explanation: Deallocated VMs stop incurring compute charges, though storage is still billed.

questions.prompt: When an Azure VM is stopped (deallocated), what are you still charged for?
questions.explanation: Deallocation stops compute billing, but the attached managed disks still incur storage charges.

questions.prompt: Which Azure subscription option is designed to let new users explore Azure with credit for a limited time?
questions.explanation: The Azure free account includes credit for the first 30 days plus some services free for a limited time or always free.

questions.prompt: What is the Azure Marketplace?
choices: A catalog where customers can find, try and buy solutions and services from Microsoft and partners
questions.explanation: Azure Marketplace offers thousands of solutions and services that are certified to run on Azure.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service lets you enforce that only specific VM SKUs can be deployed in a subscription?
questions.explanation: A policy such as Allowed virtual machine size SKUs restricts deployable VM sizes.

questions.prompt: A company wants to track who changed a network security group rule yesterday. Where should an administrator look first?
questions.explanation: The activity log records write operations on resources, including who performed them.

questions.prompt: Which tool lets you organize Azure portal views by pinning tiles and charts into custom layouts?
questions.explanation: Dashboards in the portal can be customized and shared to show key resource information.

questions.prompt: A company wants to deploy identical environments for development, test and production in a consistent, repeatable way. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Create each resource manually in the portal
Use ARM templates or Bicep files
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code templates allow repeatable, consistent deployments.

questions.prompt: Where should you look to understand how Microsoft protects data in Azure and meets standards such as GDPR and ISO 27001?
choices: Microsoft Service Trust Portal and compliance documentation
questions.explanation: The Service Trust Portal publishes audit reports and compliance information.

questions.prompt: Which tool in Microsoft Defender for Cloud gives a score showing your overall security posture?
questions.explanation: Secure score measures security posture; higher scores indicate lower risk.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure Advisor score is TRUE?
choices: It aggregates Advisor recommendations into a score showing how well resources follow best practices
It is the same as the SLA percentage
It is calculated from the number of tags
questions.explanation: Advisor score helps prioritize recommendations to improve your deployments.

questions.prompt: What does the cost analysis feature of Microsoft Cost Management let you do?
choices: Explore accumulated and forecasted costs, grouped by attributes such as resource group, service or tag
questions.explanation: Cost analysis visualizes current and forecasted spending and lets you filter and group by many attributes.

questions.prompt: Which is a benefit of applying Azure Policy at the management group level instead of each subscription?
choices: Governance is consistent across all subscriptions with a single assignment
questions.explanation: Assigning policy high in the hierarchy applies rules consistently to everything beneath.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a feature of the Azure mobile app?
choices: Replacing the Azure portal entirely for all features
Monitoring resource health and running Cloud Shell commands from a phone
questions.explanation: The Azure mobile app lets you check resource status, get alerts and use Cloud Shell on the go.

questions.prompt: Which service provides a way to restrict deletion of a critical production storage account even by administrators, until a deliberate extra step is taken?
questions.explanation: Locks require being removed before the resource can be deleted, adding a safeguard.
